title: CREATE VIEW
description: A VIEW saves a query under a name, so you can SELECT from it later like a table - the underlying query runs fresh every time, it doesn't store a copy of the data. Create a view named `pricey_products` that returns the `name` and `price` of every product priced above 30.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: CREATE VIEW
CREATE VIEW <name> AS <query> - everything after AS is a completely ordinary SELECT, it just gets saved under a name instead of run once and discarded.
Name the view pricey_products, and have its underlying SELECT return name and price from products where price is greater than 30.
expected_behavior: Creates a view that, when queried, returns name and price for products priced above 30.
solution: CREATE VIEW pricey_products AS SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 30;
explanation: A view is not a copy of the data - querying it just runs the saved SELECT again, so it always reflects the current state of the underlying tables.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT name, price FROM pricey_products ORDER BY price DESC
hidden_tests.label: pricey_products view returns the right rows
